clue.text: Lad packs nightwear

parts.note: Jim is a boy's name, standing for any lad
to pack a space is to jam it, so packs means jams

explanation.surface: A boy stuffs his pyjamas into a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Jim-jams is informal British slang for pyjamas, clothing worn in bed.

clue.text: Badly cut face in steep broken area

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit in the middle of the word for badly

parts.note: ill as an adverb means badly, as in ill-treated

indicators.note: a cut deck of cards is mixed, so the letters of face are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's face has been badly gashed in a fall on rough, steep ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' turns FACE into CEFA, and 'in' puts that inside ILL, giving I-CEFA-LL.
explanation.definitionFit: On a glacier, the steep stretch where the ice cracks into jumbled blocks is called by this name.

clue.text: Copper into 12 and I gets bath

indicators.note: the copper symbol goes inside the word from entry 12

parts.note: the clue refers to the answer at entry 12, a style of music
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Copper piping is fitted into something, and a bath results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts CU inside JAZZ (entry 12), giving JA-CU-ZZ, then I is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool bath with underwater jets is known by this trade name.

clue.text: Mafia given thus to turn up when protection's unpaid?

definitions.text: Mafia given thus to turn up when protection's unpaid?

parts.note: the Mafia is a criminal gang, a mob
something given to a person has been handed over

explanation.surface: Gangsters arrive in force when a shopkeeper has not paid protection money.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: arriving in a large intimidating group is how the gang would turn up to collect unpaid protection money.
explanation.definitionFit: Mob-handed is British slang for arriving in a large group, often to intimidate, as gangsters would.

clue.text: Explosion in pub that hurt player's technique

indicators.note: an explosion blows something apart, so the letters of pub are scattered

parts.note: ow is the cry someone gives when something hurts

explanation.surface: A blast in a bar left someone injured and crying out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosion in' rearranges PUB into UPB, then OW follows.
explanation.definitionFit: For a string player, a bow stroke starting at the tip and moving towards the frog is this technique.

clue.text: Monkey's endless enthusiasm

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the monkey's name is dropped

parts.note: the vervet is an African monkey; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A monkey shows boundless zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes the final T off VERVET.
explanation.definitionFit: Verve is vigour and spirit, a lively eagerness.

clue.text: Completely fat sexual partner one rejected

parts.note: round describes a plump, fat shape

indicators.note: rejected means this letter is thrown out of the partner's word

parts.note: a lay is slang for a sexual partner
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly overweight is spurned by a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' drops A (one) from LAY, leaving LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundly means thoroughly or in full, as in roundly condemned.

clue.text: Mix using 'Echo Baby' for such as Jardine

indicators.note: to mix something is to jumble it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A DJ produces a remix of a track called Echo Baby.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Jardine was a founding member of the Californian surf band, so he is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Jardine sang and played guitar in the American pop group famous for surf music, making him an example.

clue.text: Radiohead singer runs in harness

indicators.note: the abbreviation for runs goes inside the harness word

parts.note: a yoke is a wooden harness for oxen
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A rock vocalist goes jogging while strapped into a harness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R (runs, as in cricket scoring) inside YOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thom Yorke is the lead vocalist of the English band Radiohead.

clue.text: Transport gets Cubist moving right along

indicators.note: moving means the letter for right shifts to a new place in the painter's name

parts.note: Georges Braque was a founder of Cubism with Picasso

explanation.surface: A Cubist artist takes a vehicle and keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving ... along' shifts the R of BRAQUE one place along, giving BARQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A barque is a sailing ship, a means of carrying people or goods by sea.

clue.text: Yes to Bavarian Zones talk

parts.note: ja is German for yes, and Bavaria is a German state
Z is an abbreviation for zone, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Agreeing to a discussion in Bavarian regions.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubling an abbreviation for a plural is a convention, as pp for pages.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'all that jazz', the word can mean empty or pretentious chatter.

clue.text: Dashing hero awards points to Cupid!

indicators.note: dashing suggests rushing about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dashing hero hands out awards to the god of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points to Cupid' means Cupid's points: the sharp tips on the arrows he shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid shoots arrows, and their sharp tips are the points he uses.

clue.text: Man gone from dwelling to tend soil

indicators.note: gone from means the man's letter leaves the dwelling word

parts.note: a home is a dwelling
M is an abbreviation for man or male

explanation.surface: A man has left his house to go gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone from' takes M (man) out of HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoe is to break up earth and weed it with a long-handled garden tool.

clue.text: Complete roadside bomb connected

parts.note: all means complete or whole, as in all the way
an IED, improvised explosive device, is the typical roadside bomb

explanation.surface: A roadside bomb has gone off completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Allied means joined or linked, as in allied trades.

clue.text: Bait worm makes you throw up

definitions.meaning: the lobworm, a large earthworm used as fishing bait, shortened
to toss a ball high into the air

explanation.definitionFit: A lugworm or lobworm used by anglers shares its name with a high, looping throw, as in tennis.

clue.text: Editor and compilers turning into men after men on the side

indicators.note: into means the turned word goes inside the word for men

parts.note: men who are after other men are gay men

indicators.note: turning means the compilers' word is read backwards

parts.note: crossword compilers write of themselves as we

explanation.surface: An editor and setters gradually come round to men approaching from the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes WE into EW, and 'into' puts that inside GAYS: G-EW-AYS, after ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgeways means sideways, with the edge foremost, as in getting a word in edgeways.

clue.text: Good girl calling for fine tableware

parts.note: a lass is a girl
a calling is one's vocation or work

explanation.surface: A well-behaved girl rings up to ask for the best plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasswork covers articles made of glass, such as decanters and wine glasses set out on a table.

clue.text: Chopper's test for elevation incomplete

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: in a down answer, elevation means the letters are raised, so read bottom to top
incomplete means the test word loses its last letter

parts.note: an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A helicopter undergoes an altitude trial that is never finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' takes M off EXAM, leaving EXA, and 'for elevation' turns that upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An axe is a tool for chopping wood.

clue.text: Islands men as women wed?

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man, standing for men
women on their wedding day are brides

explanation.surface: Asking whether men might marry in the way women do.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer would mean male brides, which is what 'men as women wed' playfully describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrides are a chain of islands off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Profit by adventure

definitions.meaning: to take advantage of something, to use it for gain
a bold deed or daring feat

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to make use of something to one's gain; as a noun it is a heroic deed.

clue.text: At home on North European river

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Someone lives on a river in northern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inn flows from Switzerland through Austria into the Danube in Germany.

clue.text: Sweetener for somewhat fiery lord?

definitions.meaning: a substance added to make food sweet
Lord ..., the British businessman Alan ..., known for his gruff temper on TV's The Apprentice

explanation.definitionFit: The common sweet crystal shares its name with Alan Sugar, a hot-tempered British peer and businessman.

clue.text: Slipping bounds at court, boss makes move

indicators.note: slipping bounds means the boss word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: A judge's chief stumbles out of bounds in court and makes a motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slipping bounds' strips the first and last letters from GAFFER, leaving AFFE, then CT follows; 'at' and 'makes' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To affect someone is to stir their emotions, to touch them.

clue.text: Physicist with Royal Navy feels involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A scientist who serves with the navy feels caught up in things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' mixes RN with FEELS to make the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustin-Jean Fresnel was a French scientist known for his work on optics and his lighthouse lens.

clue.text: Foreman caught with booze reportedly

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: reportedly means the drink word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: booze is alcoholic drink, liquor

explanation.surface: A works boss is nabbed drinking on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' says LIQUOR is heard as LICKER; C comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: In shoemaking and printing, the overseer who cuts out work or makes up pages was called by this name.

clue.text: 'Modern Greats' in with long-time members

indicators.note: in means the Oxford course goes inside the word for with

parts.note: and means with, as in fish and chips
Modern Greats is the Oxford nickname for the degree PPE, philosophy, politics and economics
a long time is ages

explanation.surface: An Oxford degree course is enjoyed by long-standing members of a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts PPE inside AND, giving A-PPE-ND, then AGES. PPE is called Modern Greats at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbs and other parts attached to a body are its appendages.

clue.text: Last from Oxbridge Joke Supply

indicators.note: last from points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: a quip is a witty joke

explanation.surface: The final joke from Oxbridge undergraduates in a revue.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to provide or furnish someone with what is needed.

clue.text: Maradona to pass on success

parts.note: to pass on is to die
a go is a success, as in make a go of it

explanation.surface: A footballer passes the ball on and it comes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Diego Maradona was the celebrated Argentine footballer.

clue.text: Go without nookie

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, so without
it is a coy word for sex, as nookie is

explanation.surface: Someone is told to leave without getting any sex.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to leave or depart.

clue.text: Book some space

definitions.meaning: a single book, especially one of a set
an amount of room or capacity a thing takes up

explanation.definitionFit: The word means one tome in a series and also the cubic capacity of something.

clue.text: International snooker reserved for British South Africans

indicators.note: read as re-served, served up again in a new arrangement, the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: An international snooker table has been booked for a group of Britons in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserved' mixes I with SNOOKER. The answer is Afrikaans slang, literally 'red necks', for British South Africans.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooineks is an Afrikaans nickname, meaning red necks, for English-speaking South Africans of British descent.

clue.text: Partner's kid won't stop dancing!

parts.note: dancing is a matter of steps
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: The partner's child refuses to stop dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer suggests someone who keeps dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A child of one's spouse by an earlier relationship is a stepchild, here a boy.

clue.text: High-flyer in satellite TV job

parts.note: Sky is the British satellite television company
a lark is a jolly job or caper

explanation.surface: A star at a satellite broadcaster lands a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The skylark is a songbird famous for singing as it climbs high in the air.
